key_insight: Instead of relying on brittle per-frame intrinsic decomposition, the paper jointly learns an "environment video" representation together with a diffusion-based neural renderer so videos can be relit robustly and temporally consistently under novel illumination.
problem_solved: Current video relighting pipelines depend on accurate intrinsic decomposition (albedo, normals, illumination), which is unreliable for real-world footage and leads to distorted appearance, broken materials, and temporal artifacts when relighting.
method: Jointly learn an environment-video representation and a video neural renderer, so lighting is modeled as a temporally coherent scene-level signal rather than noisy per-frame decompositions.
Condition a large-scale video diffusion/rendering model on the learned environment video plus available geometric/color cues to synthesize frames under new illumination.
Enforce temporal consistency and appearance preservation via spatio-temporal conditioning and losses to reduce artifacts and maintain material fidelity during relighting.
impact: Makes practical, high-quality video relighting possible on in-the-wild footage without fragile intrinsic decomposition, improving realism and temporal stability for VFX, AR/VR, and content editing workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input video → joint environment-video encoder → conditioned diffusion renderer → relit output (high-level flow).
Before/after image pairs (original vs. relit) highlighting preserved materials and reduced artifacting.
Comparative chart: intrinsic-decomposition pipeline vs. joint-learning approach showing failure modes and improvements (artifacts, temporal flicker, material fidelity).
Temporal visualization: a short strip showing learned environment maps over time to illustrate coherent lighting representation.
paper_title: Relit-LiVE: Relight Video by Jointly Learning Environment Video
paper_authors: Weiqing Xiao, Hong Li, Xiuyu Yang, Houyuan Chen, Wenyi Li
